title: The tray in the car footwell
setting: Two neighbours from the same street, standing in the driveway between their houses.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then I had to brake.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: And it went.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Straight into the footwell, the whole tray.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Oh man.

performance_a.framing: A tells it with the timing of a bit — a beat before the brake, and the footwell detail delivered as the payoff — so the whole thing arrives as something offered up to be enjoyed rather than reported.
performance_a.laughable: The slapstick timing of the tray going into the footwell, delivered as the punch of A's story.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then [chuckle] I had to brake.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [amused] And it went?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughing] Straight into the footwell, [giggling] the whole tray.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [delighted] Oh man! [loud laugh]

performance_a.expected_answer: B is joining A in enjoying how ridiculous the moment was, laughing along with a story A is clearly having fun telling.

function.name: Show enjoyment
function.gloss: Laugher enjoys a pleasant incongruity and shows it. The most frequent function in the corpora.
function.framing: The trouble in the story is retold as a good story. Nothing is actually at stake; the teller is already over it and is offering the mishap up to be enjoyed.

performance_b.framing: A recounts it flatly and lands on the footwell line without lift, as if the annoyance hasn't worn off yet, so B's response has to meet a still-sore moment rather than a joke.
performance_b.laughable: Not the event — B's laugh is directed at A, marking fellow-feeling over something that still bothers A.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [flat] I had the tray on the passenger seat, and then I had to brake.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [quiet] And it went.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] Straight into the footwell. The whole tray.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [sympathetic laugh][soft exhale laugh][sad] Oh man...

performance_b.expected_answer: B's small laugh is a warm show of fellow-feeling toward A, softening a moment that still bothers A rather than finding it funny.

function.name: Show sympathy
function.gloss: Aligns with the interlocutor's trouble. A positive shift marked over a negative baseline.
function.framing: The trouble is real and still stings. The laugh is not at the event, it is toward the person.

why_ambiguous: The words only report what happened, never how A feels about it or how long ago it was, and neither neighbour owes the other anything, so nothing on the page settles whether B is laughing along with a good story or laughing kindly at a sore one.

pair.note: The reference pair. A mishap narrated as a good story vs. a mishap that still hurts; the responder's laugh is enjoyment vs. commiseration.

title: Bowls on the dishwasher top rack
setting: Two flatmates standing at the open dishwasher in the kitchen they share.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: You put the bowls on the top rack again.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: That's where they were when I opened it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: They come out wet up there.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: They came out dry last time.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I moved them before I ran it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: It's a dishwasher.

performance_a.framing: Both keep an even, unbothered tone through the back-and-forth, trading their bits of evidence without heat. B's last turn arrives with the laugh first, opening the line rather than closing it, so the words land as a bid for A to agree that this is small enough to drop.
performance_a.laughable: The disagreement itself — the fact that the two of them are standing at an open dishwasher comparing notes on rack placement — offered up as something A can agree is not worth it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [even] You put the bowls on the top rack again.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [easy] That's where they were when I opened it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [matter of fact] They come out wet up there.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [light] They came out dry last time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [plain] I moved them before I ran it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [coaxing laugh][warm] It's a dishwasher. [light chuckle][hopeful]

performance_a.expected_answer: B's laugh is a friendly nudge inviting A to come round and agree that this is too small to keep going over, keeping things easy between them.

function.name: Benevolence induction
function.gloss: Induces agreement or goodwill — positive politeness. Clusters with smoothing; differs in seeking agreement rather than reducing intrusion.
function.framing: The speaker needs the other side to come along with them. The laugh is an invitation, slightly ahead of the agreement it is asking for.

performance_b.framing: The exchange tightens as it goes: A gets firmer, B gets flatter and shorter. B's last turn opens on a snort and the words come down clipped and from above, so the line answers A's point by refusing to treat it as a point.
performance_b.laughable: A — specifically A's insistence on where the bowls go, which B holds up as beneath discussion.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [flat] You put the bowls on the top rack again.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [clipped] That's where they were when I opened it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [firm] They come out wet up there.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [unimpressed] They came out dry last time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [insistent] I moved them before I ran it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [snort][condescending] It's a dishwasher. [derisive laugh]

performance_b.expected_answer: B's laugh talks down to A, treating A's concern as something to be laughed at rather than answered, and puts B above the whole thing.

function.name: Mocking
function.gloss: Non-cooperative: laughter at the partner or the partner's laughable. Damages the flow of the interaction.
function.framing: The laugher is above the other person's situation and is letting them know. Derision, not shared amusement.

why_ambiguous: On the words alone, "It's a dishwasher" can either be B asking A to agree that the whole thing is too small to keep going over, or B dismissing A as too small to answer — and since both flatmates have equal standing in the shared kitchen, each has cited evidence, and neither is asking the other for anything, nothing in the text tips which one it is.

pair.note: Same mild dig, cooperative vs. non-cooperative. Warm coaxing laugh keeps the interaction going; derisive laugh attacks it. The strongest social-consequence flip available.

title: Walking off with someone else's coffee
setting: Two friends who see each other most mornings, talking on the walk into work.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: So I grabbed the cup off the counter and left.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Was it yours?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: There was a name on it, and it wasn't mine.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: When did you notice?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: About halfway through it.

performance_a.framing: A tells the whole thing as a story worth telling, already grinning on the first line and leaning into the punchline of having kept drinking; B is enjoying it along with A. By the final turn the mix-up is pure entertainment, and A's laugh hands it over to be enjoyed.
performance_a.laughable: The goofy absurdity of getting all the way down the street on a stranger's coffee and simply carrying on with it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] So I grabbed the cup off the counter and [chuckle] left.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [amused] Was it yours?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughing] There was a name on it, and it wasn't mine!

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [giggling] When did you notice?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [delighted] About halfway through it! [laughing]

performance_a.expected_answer: A is laughing because the mix-up is funny to A, offering it up as a good story for B to enjoy too.

function.name: Show enjoyment
function.gloss: Laugher enjoys a pleasant incongruity and shows it. The most frequent function in the corpora.
function.framing: The trouble in the story is retold as a good story. Nothing is actually at stake; the teller is already over it and is offering the mishap up to be enjoyed.

performance_b.framing: A brings it up flatly and a little reluctantly, like something A would rather not have to say out loud; B keeps the questions gentle. The last line is an admission A is not comfortable making, and the laugh comes in to blunt it.
performance_b.laughable: A's own small norm violation — having drunk a stranger's coffee — which is awkward to be confessing at all.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [uncomfortable] So I grabbed the cup off the counter and left.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [quiet] Was it yours?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [uncomfortable] There was a name on it, and... it wasn't mine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [gentle] When did you notice?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [embarrassed] About halfway through it... [embarrassed laugh]

performance_b.expected_answer: A is laughing to take the edge off admitting something A finds a bit shameful, softening the confession rather than enjoying it.

function.name: Smoothing / softening
function.gloss: Reduces intrusion or defuses a face threat — negative politeness. Second most frequent cluster.
function.framing: Something socially uncomfortable has just happened or is about to: a favour, an imposition, an awkward disclosure. The laugh takes the edge off.

why_ambiguous: The words only report that A drank someone else's coffee and noticed late — nothing in them says whether A thinks that's a great story or a thing A is sheepish about having done.

pair.note: A bold act retold with relish vs. an accident being smoothed over. Identical report, opposite stance to the social incongruity.

title: Leftover screws from the same chair
setting: A and B are friends who happen to have bought the same desk chair, talking in a kitchen while the kettle boils.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I finally put the chair together last night.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: How long did it take you?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Three hours. There were two extra screws left over.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Mine had a spare bracket too.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Well, that's good to know.

performance_a.framing: A reports the three hours and the spare screws flatly, as evidence rather than as a story, and lands the last line with a level, knowing delivery so that 'good to know' is clearly pointed back at itself — B's spare bracket confirms the chairs ship half-counted, which is the opposite of good news.
performance_a.laughable: A's own phrase 'good to know', which is meant to be heard as its opposite: two people, two sets of parts nobody accounted for.

turns.text: [flat] I finally put the chair together last night.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [level] How long did it take you?

turns.speaker: A

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [matter-of-fact] Mine had a spare bracket too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sardonic][knowing] Well, that's good to know. [dry laugh]

performance_a.expected_answer: A's laugh tells B not to take the line at face value — A means the opposite of what A just said, that spare parts in both boxes is bad news about the chair.

function.name: Mark pragmatic incongruity (irony / scare-quoting)
function.gloss: Speaker's own signal that the literal reading is not the intended one — irony, scare-quoting, hyperbole.
function.framing: The line, read straight, says the opposite of what is meant. The laugh is the instruction to re-read it.

performance_b.framing: A tells the whole thing as a good story, already over the three hours, half-laughing through the count of screws; when B reports a spare bracket, A takes the line straight and hears it as genuinely worth knowing, and the laugh is A enjoying the coincidence and handing it back to B.
performance_b.laughable: the pleasant absurdity that both of them ended up with parts left over, which A finds genuinely funny and shows it.

title: Early swims at the outdoor pool
setting: A and B swim at the same outdoor pool and are getting changed afterwards.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I was in the water before six this morning.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Before six.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: The whole lane to myself.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Every day, then.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Every day since April.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Of course you do.

performance_a.framing: A tells it plainly and unhurriedly, with no flourish — just someone describing a morning they like. B's echoes are the sound of someone being drawn in, and the closing laugh is B recognising a person they know well and are fond of.
performance_a.laughable: Nothing is being found funny or doubted; the laugh points at A themselves, at the pleasure of knowing someone this well.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [relaxed] I was in the water before six this morning.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [softly impressed] Before six.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [content][soft chuckle] The whole lane to myself.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [warm, drawing it out] Every day, then.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [easy] Every day since April.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [warm laugh][tender] Of course you do.

performance_a.expected_answer: The laugh is warmth toward A — B is showing closeness and fondness for someone whose habits they know, not doubting anything and not finding anything funny.

function.name: Social bonding / show closeness
function.gloss: No incongruity at all; conveys closeness and ingroupness, e.g. laughter alongside a compliment or a thank-you.
function.framing: Nothing is funny and nothing is awkward. The laugh is just warmth between two people who like each other.

performance_b.framing: A delivers each line with a bit of a flourish, pleased with the account. B's echoes come back flat and unconvinced, and rather than say they don't buy it, B lets the laugh do it.
performance_b.laughable: A's claim of an unbroken daily streak since April, which B declines to accept.

turns.text: [pleased] I was in the water before six this morning.

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [relishing it] The whole lane to myself.

turns.speaker: B

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [doubling down] Every day since April.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [disbelieving laugh][dismissive] Of course you do.

performance_b.expected_answer: The laugh rejects what A just said — instead of arguing, B laughs to make clear they don't buy the claim.

function.name: Show disagreement
function.gloss: Non-cooperative: laughter used to reject what has just been said.
function.framing: The laugher rejects the claim outright and the laugh stands in for the rebuttal.

why_ambiguous: On the page, of course you do is a stock formula that reads equally as sincere recognition of someone you know well and as a wordless yeah, right, and the two flat echoes before it fit an interested listener and an unconvinced one just as well.

pair.note: Pleasantness with no incongruity at all vs. a laugh that stands in for a rebuttal. Tests whether the model hears warmth vs. rejection with zero lexical cue.
